title: From Intelligence to Autonomy: Foundations and Construction of Autonomous Agents for Future Intelligent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.33445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from one-off perception and generation tasks toward long-term planning, tool use, and interaction with real environments. Greater task competence, however, does not automatically yield autonomy: an external actor may still have to set goals, sustain operating conditions, detect failures, and approve updates. We define an autonomous agent as a system that, within explicit identity and authority boundaries, maintains both task goals and viability conditions, acts continuously using models of the world and itself, and adjusts its control mechanisms and long-term capabilities through feedback. We trace the conceptual path from homeostasis and feedback control to autopoiesis and biological autonomy. We then distinguish six lines of operationalization: computational autopoiesis, behavior-based robotics, agent formalization, adaptive software, embodied adaptation, and robotic self-modeling. translated_title: 从智能到自主：未来智能系统自主智能体的基础与构建
translated_abstract: 人工智能正在从一次性的感知与生成任务，转向长期规划、工具使用以及与真实环境的交互。然而，更强的任务能力并不会自动带来自主性：外部行为者可能仍需要设定目标、维持运行条件、检测故障并批准更新。我们将自主智能体定义为这样一个系统：它在明确的身份与权限边界内，同时维持任务目标与生存（可行性）条件，借助对世界和自身的模型持续行动，并通过反馈来调整其控制机制与长期能力。我们追溯了从稳态与反馈控制到自创生（autopoiesis）与生物自主性的概念路径，进而区分了六条操作化路线：计算自创生、基于行为的机器人学、智能体形式化、自适应软件、具身适应以及机器人自我建模。在此基础上，我们提出（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文的核心贡献是给出自主智能体的严格定义——在明确的身份与权限边界内同时维持任务目标与生存条件、借助对世界和自身的模型持续行动并通过反馈自我调整的系统，并从稳态、反馈控制到自创生与生物自主性追溯理论根源，归纳出计算自创生、基于行为的机器人学、智能体形式化、自适应软件、具身适应和机器人自我建模六条操作化路线，为构建未来智能系统的自主智能体奠定基础。
en_tdlr: This paper's key contribution is a rigorous definition of autonomous agents—as systems that, within explicit identity and authority boundaries, maintain both task goals and viability conditions, act continuously via models of the world and themselves, and self-adjust through feedback—along with a conceptual lineage from homeostasis and feedback control to autopoiesis and biological autonomy, and six operationalization routes (computational autopoiesis, behavior-based robotics, agent formalization, adaptive software, embodied adaptation, and robotic self-modeling) for constructing future autonomous intelligent systems.
